puzzles.title: Use the Hill-cipher inverse matrix
puzzles.prompt:
Alphabet: ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ12345
Supplied inverse matrix:
  [12  6]
  [12  2]
Ciphertext blocks: QB RA EO ME

For each block, convert the two letters to their numeric values (A=0..5=30), multiply by the inverse matrix modulo 31, convert back to letters, then join all blocks and remove the trailing filler.
puzzles.hint:
How to use the inverse matrix:
1. Number the alphabet from 0 to 30: A=0, ..., Z=25, 1=26, ..., 5=30.
2. Read the ciphertext two characters at a time. For each pair, use its two numbers as a column vector.
3. Multiply that vector by the supplied inverse matrix. `mod 31` means keep the remainder after division by 31, so every result returns to the alphabet range.

Unrelated example using the same matrix: LB -> OK.
L=11 and B=1, so the vector is [11, 1].
First letter: (12 x 11 + 6 x 1) = 138; 138 mod 31 = 14; 14 -> O.
Second letter: (12 x 11 + 2 x 1) = 134; 134 mod 31 = 10; 10 -> K.
Repeat that process for each ciphertext block, then remove a final filler `3`.

metadata.web_prompt: Use the inverse matrix to decode the ciphertext blocks.

chapters.title: Chapter 3: 5 MINUTES LEFT TO LIVE
chapters.description: Chapter 3: decode a Morse signal then crack a Caesar cipher to find the report code.

puzzles.title: Read the urgent signal
puzzles.prompt:
Morse transmission:
.... ..- .-. .-. -.--

Decode the single word.
puzzles.hint: Use the Morse-code reference below. Decode each space-separated character.

puzzles.title: Decode the encrypted message
puzzles.prompt:
Encrypted message:
WKH VDPH OHWWHU DSSHDUV RIWHQ LQ HQJOLVK. WKH PHVVDJH RSHQV ZKHQ BRX WHVW FRPPRQ ZRUGV. UHSRUW FRGH: HDVW JDWH.

Decode the full message.
puzzles.hint:
Ranked letter counts:
  H: 17 (19.10%)
  W: 10 (11.24%)
  V:  9 (10.11%)
  R:  8 ( 8.99%)
  D:  6 ( 6.74%)
  Q:  6 ( 6.74%)
  U:  5 ( 5.62%)
  K:  4 ( 4.49%)
  P:  4 ( 4.49%)
  S:  4 ( 4.49%)

Clue 1 — In English, E is the most common letter. H appears most often in the encrypted message, so H likely stands for E.
Clue 2 — WKH appears as a word. THE is the most common three-letter word in English (W->T, K->H, H->E).
Both clues point to a Caesar cipher: shift each letter back by 3.

metadata.web_prompt: Decode the encrypted message to find the report code at the end.
metadata.web_hint:

Clue 2 — WKH appears as a word, so think of the most common three-letter word in English
Both clues point to a Caesar cipher. Recap: a Caesar cipher shifts each letter by a fixed amount
